q: In Tripartite Agreement, formula for calculating of amount of LC/BG is :

options.A: Total freight during the last financial year/Actual days of transaction in concerned month x 2.
options.B: Total freight during the last financial year/Actual days of transaction in concerned year x 2.
options.C: Total freight during the last two financial year/Actual days of transaction in concerned month x 2.

e: Total freight during the last financial year/Actual days of transaction in concerned month x 2. — that is the right answer. Under the Tripartite Agreement, the LC/BG amount equals the total freight of the last financial year divided by the actual days of transaction in the concerned month, multiplied by two. This covers roughly two days of freight as security for e-payment transactions. The amount is revised after every financial year's transactions. The LC/BG protects the railway against default in electronic freight payment.

q: What does ‘OR’ in the Railway Receipt indicate
e: This question turns on a precise definition — here is the reasoning. OR in the Railway Receipt indicates Owner's Risk. Goods accepted at owner's risk are carried with limited railway liability — compensation is payable only for loss or damage proved to be due to the railway's misconduct or negligence. q: What is the full form of GCC ?
e: The correct answer is Goods Compensation Claims.. GCC stands for Goods Compensation Claims. These are claims for loss, destruction, damage, deterioration or non-delivery of goods in transit, lodged under Section 106 of the Railways Act, 1989. Records of compensation claims are preserved for six years as per Appendix IX. Post check applies to claims up to Rs. 75,000. q: Customer entrusting any Goods to Railway for carriage shall execute in a specific form called
e: Option B (Forwarding Note) is the correct choice. A customer entrusting goods to the railway for carriage must execute a Forwarding Note in the prescribed form. The forwarding note declares the consignment details — description, weight, consignor and consignee — and is the basis for issuing the Railway Receipt. It is tendered at the time of registration of the wagon demand. Correct declaration in the forwarding note avoids mis-declaration penalties.

q: Charges levied for hauling a rake (freight Train) between Railway serving station and its siding for loading/unloading of goods are
e: The correct answer is Siding charges. Charges levied for hauling a rake between the railway serving station and its siding for loading or unloading of goods are siding charges. They are computed by the trip-time method with a minimum of one hour. Siding charges at the originating point are compulsorily collected along with freight. They are distinct from shunting charges, which cover engine shunting of wagons.
